messages:
Mei (Engineer): quick q 111 i bought an international eSIM and a 5-day pocket wifi for a customer trip. can we reimburse both?
Carlos (Sales): our last trip we just expense the cheapest connectivity since we were with 3 people. finance asked for split proof.
Avery (People Ops): general rules? single traveler vs team device?
Lian (Finance): short answer: connectivity costs that are business-related are reimbursable. differences: 1) personal phone data plans (monthly recurring) are not auto reimbursable; 2) single-use eSIMs or day passes purchased specifically for travel are reimbursable with receipt and reason; 3) pocket wifi/hotspot rental for a group is reimbursable but you must allocate per-person or show justification that device was used for business (e.g., shared vendor demo).
ITAdmin: also note: for recurring travel, IT can order corporate eSIMs or temporary SIMs tied to a company-owned device. that avoids monthly personal-plan reimbursement and simplifies billing. talk to IT before buying if you travel frequently.
Mei (Engineer): what counts as "business-related"? i used the pocket wifi to demo to the client and to run remote tests for 3 days.
Lian (Finance): that's business-related. attach a one-line justification: "used to demo X to Client Y on dates" and upload the original purchase invoice + any QR code confirmation from the eSIM provider. we accept screenshots from vendor portals only if they clearly show purchaser, date, and amount.
Carlos (Sales): team device scenario: if 4 people share a pocket wifi and one person paid, how should we file?
Lian (Finance): preferred: the payer uploads the receipt and a short allocation note listing each claimant's share and business reason. example: "Pocket wifi $60 total; attendees A/B/C/D; Business share per person $15." Attach event invite or meeting notes as supporting context.
Mei (Engineer): i bought an eSIM via an app that auto-renewed after a week (i canceled but got charged again). can we get that second charge reimbursed?
Lian (Finance): recurring charges are evaluated case-by-case. we reimburse travel purchases when they are one-off and business-related. if an auto-renew happens in error, show evidence you attempted cancellation and the vendor's refund policy. Finance may reimburse the pro-rated business portion if you can show travel dates that match. avoid recurring plans without preapproval.
Avery (People Ops): any limits on cost or preferred vendors? we had someone buy an expensive unlimited plan last month.
Lian (Finance): keep it reasonable. for single trips we expect pay-as-you-go or short term passes. if you need an expensive plan for business-critical reasons, get manager + People Ops preapproval. Finance reserves the right to cap reimbursements for connectivity at a reasonable market rate and will ask for justification for outliers.
ITAdmin: note for device rentals: if the pocket wifi is company-requested for a customer demo or vendor install, IT can pre-approve vendor rentals. use the internal procurement channel for bookings > $200.
Mei (Engineer): what about taxes/VAT on the vendor site? provider was EU-based with VAT included. how do we submit?
Lian (Finance): upload the vendor invoice that shows VAT. Finance will attempt to reclaim VAT where eligible for company-paid expenses. if portion is personal (e.g., companion or personal days) that VAT portion remains personal. include card statement for FX conversion if needed.
Carlos (Sales): can we buy a single SIM and hand it across the team across trips (company-owned)?
ITAdmin: yes, company-owned SIMs/devices are preferred for repeated team travel. IT will track inventory and bill to departmental cost center. submit a request to IT and include travel schedule; they can provision with data bundles.
Mei (Engineer): file naming/attachments?
Lian (Finance): name attachments like `lastname_1795003210_esim_invoice.jpg` and `lastname_1795003210_wifi_receipt.pdf`. include one-line justification in the expense form and manager approval screenshot `lastname_1795003210_manager_ok.png` when applicable.
ExpenseBot: POLICY HIGHLIGHT 1: Temporary travel connectivity (eSIM, day passes, pocket wifi) is reimbursable when directly business-related with original receipt + justification. Recurring/mobile subscriptions require preapproval and may not be reimbursed. Company-owned devices should be requested via IT for repeat use.
Avery (People Ops): TL;DR 1: buy temporary passes for single trips, share/rent devices with allocation note, avoid recurring plans without preapproval. i'll add a short checklist in #docs and ping IT about a team device pool.
Mei (Engineer): perfect, thanks! submitting now. :thumbsup:
Carlos (Sales): thanks everyone :rocket:
